items.stem: How should a strategist use the 'hype cycle' when assessing an emerging technology?

options.text: As a critical narrative aid about expectation patterns, not a precise predictor of timing or success
options.rationale: Correct: the hype cycle illustrates expectation dynamics but does not reliably predict outcomes or dates.

options.text: As an exact forecast of when a technology will become profitable
options.rationale: It is not a precise timing or profitability forecast.

options.text: As proof that any hyped technology will certainly succeed
options.rationale: Hype does not guarantee success; many hyped technologies fade.

options.text: As a reason to ignore all new technologies
options.rationale: It is an analytical aid, not a reason to dismiss everything.

items.explanation: Correct: the hype cycle illustrates expectation dynamics but does not reliably predict outcomes or dates.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound foresight practices? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Triangulating weak signals across multiple independent sources
options.rationale: Correct: corroborating signals across sources reduces false positives.

options.text: Developing multiple scenarios to stress-test strategy
options.rationale: Correct: scenarios test robustness against several plausible futures.

options.text: Committing fully to a single predicted future
options.rationale: Over-committing to one forecast is fragile under uncertainty.

options.text: Treating a single viral headline as confirmed fact
options.rationale: One unverified headline is not a validated signal.

items.explanation: Correct: corroborating signals across sources reduces false positives.

items.stem: Why are scenarios, rather than a single forecast, valuable in technology foresight?

options.text: They stress-test strategy against several plausible futures, exposing risks and robust options
options.rationale: Correct: multiple scenarios reveal which choices hold up across different futures.

options.text: Because they predict exactly which future will occur
options.rationale: Scenarios are not point predictions of the one true future.

options.text: Because they remove all uncertainty from planning
options.rationale: Scenarios manage uncertainty; they do not eliminate it.

options.text: Because they let you ignore risks entirely
options.rationale: Scenarios surface risks rather than letting you ignore them.

items.explanation: Correct: multiple scenarios reveal which choices hold up across different futures.
